newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed in slow late trading on Monday on the back of relatively adequate liquidity, dealers said.
They said trading was featureless due to a public holiday in the United States and lack of fresh domestic leads.
"We haven't got any request from overseas since the opening, the market is very quiet on lack of fresh news," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Dealers said operators were also seen looking for possible interesting developments from the regular monthly cabinet meeting scheduled for Wednesday.
"Operators are looking for some fresh leads from the regular cabinet meeting as the importance of the ongoing Megawati case seems to have diminished," another bank dealer said.
Megawati Sukarnoputri, deposed leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), has sued the government for ousting her from the leadership of the PDI.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,342.20/42.50, compared with an opening of 2,342.60/43.10.
The dealer said the dollar-rupiah rate was likely to stay little changed on Tuesday on lack of fresh leads.
One-month swap was at 16.70/16.90, two at 34.00/35.00, three at 51.75/52.25 and six at 103.00/103.75 points.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,341/2,459 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,341/2,387 on Monday.
